title: Epidemiology and Clinical Characteristics of IgA Vasculitis with Renal Involvement – A Prospective Observational Study
summary:
IgA vasculitis is a disease in which small blood vessels become inflamed. The disease is caused by the deposition of a type of antibody called immunoglobulin A (IgA) in the walls of blood vessels and in different organs. IgA vasculitis is the most common form of systemic vasculitis in children. Typical symptoms include a red or purple, raised skin rash that can be felt when touching the skin, joint pain, abdominal pain, and changes in kidney function. In adults, IgA vasculitis is less common than in children. However, kidney involvement occurs more frequently and is often more severe in older children and adults. Men are affected more often than women. When the kidneys are affected, IgA-containing deposits can accumulate in the kidneys and cause inflammation. The changes seen in a kidney tissue sample under the microscope can be very similar to those seen in another kidney disease called IgA nephropathy. Although these two diseases are closely related, it is currently not fully understood why some patients develop IgA vasculitis and others develop IgA nephropathy. There are currently no sufficiently established treatment recommendations for IgA vasculitis with kidney involvement. This is mainly because there have been only a limited number of clinical studies comparing different treatments. Depending on the severity of the disease, treatment may include medication to protect kidney function, such as ACE inhibitors or SGLT2 inhibitors, as well as measures such as reducing salt intake and stopping smoking. In some patients with significant protein loss in the urine, treatment with corticosteroids may be considered. In patients with a particularly severe and rapidly worsening inflammation of the kidneys, stronger treatments such as corticosteroids combined with other medicines may be necessary.

The aim of this study is to improve our understanding of IgA vasculitis, particularly when the kidneys are affected. For this purpose, we will collect and evaluate information about the symptoms, laboratory results, kidney function, treatments, and the course of the disease. If a kidney biopsy has been performed as part of routine medical care, the findings will also be evaluated. In addition, blood and urine samples will be examined in the laboratory. The aim is to identify measurable substances, known as biomarkers, that may provide information about the presence or severity of the disease or help predict how the disease will develop. Existing information from follow-up examinations will also be used to investigate the long-term course of the disease and kidney function. This will allow us to examine whether certain clinical findings, laboratory values, or treatments are associated with a better or worse outcome. The results of the study are intended to improve the understanding of IgA vasculitis with kidney involvement and, in the long term, to contribute to the development of better and more evidence-based treatment strategies.

This is a prospective observational study. This means that patients with IgA vasculitis and patients with IgA nephropathy will be followed over time and their disease course will be documented. The study consists of two groups: one group of patients with IgA vasculitis and one group of patients with IgA nephropathy. The two groups will be compared in order to identify similarities and differences between the two diseases, particularly with regard to kidney involvement and the further course of the disease. The study does not involve any experimental treatment. There will therefore be no random assignment to different treatment groups and no blinding. All examinations and treatment decisions will be made according to the usual medical care and will not be changed because of participation in the study. The blood and urine samples will be used exclusively for the scientific investigations described in the study. The laboratory analyses may include measurements of disease-related substances. No genetic testing will be performed.
